question: What happens to the decomposition rate when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin?
solution:
The correct answer is__** It is slower.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The following **variables influence **the rate of decomposition:

 
 
• 
 **Chemical **make-up of detritus,
 
 
• 
 **pH**,
 
 
• 
 **Temperature**,
 
 
• 
 **Moisture, **and
 
 
• 
 **Aeration **of the **soil**.
 
 
 
 
• 
 Decomposition **proceeds **more **quickly **when the soil is **rich **in **nitrogen**.
 
 
• 
 The rate of decomposition is **accelerated **by the presence of **water**-**soluble carbohydrates**.
 
 
• 
 The degradation process is **slowed **down by the presence of big complex polymers in the debris, like** lignin and chitin.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **breakdown** of **dead organic **matter into more **fundamental organic **or **inorganic **components including carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars, and mineral salts is known as decomposition, also referred to as rot.
 
• The process, which is a part of the **nutrient cycle**, is essential for recycling the scant material that occupies space in the biosphere.
 
• When a living organism passes away, the body begins to **decompose**.
 
• **Animals **like worms also contribute to the **breakdown **of the **chemical molecules**.
 
• Organisms that carry out this process are known as **decomposers **or **detritivores**.
